title: QR-Code Phishing
overview: Inspect a normalized URL verdict for a redirect discovered during QR inspection.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A QR-derived redirect classified as a credential lure supports a message and click investigation.
evidence: Review the QR origin, redirect verdict and message identifier. Correlate the recipient’s activity without using the URL.
false_positive: A legitimate event registration or facilities email can also contain a redirecting QR code.
tuning: Use destination and redirect context. Avoid treating every QR code as suspicious.
response: Quarantine related messages, check interactions and review sign-ins if recipients used the destination.
prevention: Use QR inspection and phishing-resistant authentication. Teach users to report unexpected QR sign-in prompts.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: No QR image, active URL or credential collection appears in the fixture.

questions.prompt: Which evidence distinguishes the fixture from a normal QR message?
options: A redirect verdict indicating a credential lure
The presence of a QR code alone
questions.explanation: QR format is a delivery detail. Destination analysis gives the signal.

questions.prompt: Where could an analyst find follow-on impact?
questions.explanation: A delivery verdict cannot establish whether a recipient interacted.
